newsitem.title: FRANCE: France Telecom staff urged to buy shares.
newsitem.headline: France Telecom staff urged to buy shares.

text.p: France Telecom SA is doing all it can to encourage its 164,620 staff to become shareholders and overcome remaining employee opposition to the partial privatisation next month.
Labour union representatives told Reuters on Tuesday that the shareholder plans appeared far more attractive than those used at other companies during their market introduction.
The France Telecom offer has four schemes. Abondix and Multiplix fall within a company savings plan and will be exempt from tax on dividends and asset gains.
The schemes vary in the amounts invested and in incentives. With Abondix, France Telecom adds part of the sum invested and gives right to additional shares after three years.
Multiplix offers a guaranteed gain of 25 percent.
Under Simplix, staff have to keep the shares for at least two years and dividend and asset gains are taxable.
For these three schemes staff can buy shares at a 20 percent discount to the IPO price.

A fourth scheme, Disponix, makes the shares immediately available to staff and they can also directly be sold. But if staff hold the shares for a year there will be bonus shares. With Disponix there is no discount.
The Communist-led CGT union said that France Telecom and the state were "pulling out all stops" to "create the example of popular support for the sale".

"I believe that the aim of having staff-shareholders is to integrate the civil servants in the logic of an economic framework -- that is, to look at the share price rather than defend their rights," a CGT representative said.
"The favourable conditions are aimed at shutting up any action by employees for their demands," he added.
Spokesmen at the Force Ouvriere and SUD unions underlined that at the recent staff representative elections, 60 percent of the votes went to FO and CGT, which are opposed to the sale.
CGT and SUD have told their members to refuse the offers of buying shares.

"The obvious interpretation of these favourable conditions to buy shares is that the management of France Telecom wants to get a favourable answer from the staff and that the 10 percent of shares reserved for staff will find an easy buyer," an FO union representative said.
At SUD, a representative said that the staff share buy schemes were very important politically.

"For the management of France Telecom, it is very important politically that there is a massive participation by the staff," he said explaining that the company could then claim that despite the staff representative election results there was majority support for the partial privatisation.
